rationale.usefulness: Linked app views, permission-checked references and direct local endpoints form a practical database-to-interface workflow for existing Datasette users. The report specifies instructor answer keys, forbidden-record checks, missing data, browser navigation, removed grants and accessibility tests, with an inspectable SQL-to-record video example. It also identifies actionable patched versions and credential configuration. No learning, cost or runtime benefit is claimed without testing.
rationale.impact: The November 14–15 changes improve an existing ecosystem through linkable views, a homepage prompt, endpoint configuration and permission corrections. These are valuable operational refinements, particularly for local-model users, but the saved release notes do not demonstrate a new general AI capability or a domain-wide performance advance. A below-five impact rating reflects this incremental scope, independently of the report length.
rationale.novelty: Fragment manifests discoverable by app_links and direct endpoint dictionaries meaningfully integrate established browser navigation and model-service mechanisms into Datasette. The report does not portray URL fragments, OpenAI-compatible endpoints or permission grants as newly invented techniques. Demonstrated differentiation is mainly workflow composition and reduced configuration friction within an existing product.
rationale.maturity: Tagged releases and detailed current documentation expose concrete behavior, dependencies and failure boundaries, supporting a usable-with-limits score. However Agent, Apps, datasette-llm and Datasette 1.0a43 remain prereleases, recent permission/configuration bugs require attention, and no combined installation or local-model compatibility test was performed. The report accurately distinguishes stopping from rollback, documentation from enforcement testing, and HTML sandbox scope from unrestricted Python plugins.
rationale.openness: Saved Agent and Apps LICENSE pages identify Apache 2.0; public repositories, stored SQL/app source and configurable OpenAI-compatible endpoints support inspection and portability. The report keeps dataset and model-service rights separate. Dependence on a compatible tool-calling model, alpha package combinations and untested integration prevents claiming exceptional reproducibility or universal local-server support.
